F1.quote: We present OLMoTrace, the first system that traces the outputs of language models back to their full, multi-trillion-token training data in real time.
F1.claim: OLMoTrace defined by its authors: the first system to trace language-model outputs back to their full, multi-trillion-token training data in real time
F1.lineage: what it is: tracing model output to its training data in real time

F2.quote: Today we introduce OLMoTrace, a one-of-a-kind feature in the Ai2 Playground that lets you trace the outputs of language models back to their full, multi-trillion-token training data in real time.
F2.claim: the operator's post introduces it as a feature of the Ai2 Playground that traces model outputs to their full training data in real time
F2.lineage: what it is: tracing model output to its training data in real time

F3.quote: OLMoTrace finds and shows verbatim matches between segments of language model output and documents in the training text corpora.
F3.claim: what it finds: verbatim matches between segments of model output and documents in the training corpora
F3.lineage: the relation: verbatim match between output and training text

F4.quote: The highlights indicate long and unique spans that appear verbatim at least once in the training data of this model.
F4.claim: the highlighted spans are long and unique spans that occur verbatim at least once in the model's training data
F4.lineage: the relation: verbatim match between output and training text

F5.locus: §6 Related Work, 'Tracing LM generation into training data'
F5.quote: we directly retrieve similar training examples by lexical overlap, with the heuristic that such training examples are likely to be influential for the given output.
F5.claim: its method against influence functions: retrieval by lexical overlap, on the heuristic that such examples are likely to be influential
F5.lineage: the relation: verbatim match between output and training text

F6.quote: The purpose of OLMoTrace is to give users a tool to explore where LMs may have learned to generate certain word sequences, focusing on verbatim matching as the most direct connection between LM outputs and the training data.
F6.claim: its purpose: to explore where models may have learned to generate word sequences, verbatim matching taken as the most direct connection
F6.lineage: purpose: where a model may have learned a word sequence

F7.quote: We developed OLMoTrace to enable researchers, developers, and the general public to inspect where and how language models may have learned to generate certain word sequences.
F7.claim: developed so that researchers, developers and the public can inspect where and how models may have learned word sequences
F7.lineage: purpose: where a model may have learned a word sequence

F8.quote: We are still in an early stage in exploring the full potential of this tool
F8.claim: the operator places the tool at an early stage of exploring its potential
F8.lineage: purpose: where a model may have learned a word sequence

F9.quote: reducing the time complexity of span finding from the naive O(L^2 * N) to O(L * log N)
F9.claim: span finding over an infini-gram index, its time complexity reduced from O(L^2 * N) to O(L * log N)
F9.lineage: the pipeline: spans, index, retrieval, ranking

F10.quote: For each kept span, we retrieve up to 10 document snippets from the training data that enclose this span. … we rank all documents by a BM25 score in descending order.
F10.claim: up to 10 enclosing document snippets retrieved per kept span; the documents ranked by BM25
F10.lineage: the pipeline: spans, index, retrieval, ranking

F11.quote: We find that this BM25 score conveys some notion of “relevance”, and thus we surface documents with higher scores on top.
F11.claim: the BM25 ranking conveys 'some notion of relevance'
F11.lineage: the pipeline: spans, index, retrieval, ranking

F12.quote: After generating an answer from OLMo in the Ai2 Playground, users can activate the tool by clicking the “Show OLMoTrace” button below the output.
F12.claim: activated in the Playground by the 'Show OLMoTrace' button below a model's answer
F12.lineage: the pipeline: spans, index, retrieval, ranking

F13.quote: the OLMoTrace inference latency per query is 4.46 seconds
F13.claim: measured latency: 4.46 seconds per query on 98 internal conversations

F14.quote: The first document displayed in each conversation received an average relevance score of 1.90 (roughly meaning “being on the same topic as the LM output)
F14.claim: the first displayed document scored 1.90 of 3 on human-rated relevance, roughly 'on the same topic'

F15.quote: which totals 3.2 billion documents and 4.6 trillion (Llama-2) tokens
F15.claim: OLMo-2-32B-Instruct's training data, matched in full: 3.2 billion documents, 4.6 trillion tokens
F15.lineage: the training data and its count

F16.quote: In total, these five datasets contain about 3.2 billion documents and 4.6 trillion tokens, and OLMoTrace matches against all of them.
F16.claim: the five datasets of pre-, mid- and post-training, about 3.2 billion documents and 4.6 trillion tokens, all matched
F16.lineage: the training data and its count

F17.quote: OLMoTrace is available today with our three flagship models: OLMo 2 32B Instruct, OLMo 2 13B Instruct, and OLMoE 1B 7B Instruct, and it can be applied to any language model for which you have access to the training data.
F17.claim: at launch three models (OLMo 2 32B and 13B Instruct, OLMoE 1B 7B Instruct); applicable to any model whose training data one has access to

F18.quote: Olmo 3 is wired into OlmoTrace in the Ai2 Playground, so you don't just see its behavior—you can trace it. For example, you can ask Olmo 3-Think (32B
F18.claim: Ai2 on X: OLMo 3 traced in the Playground, OLMo 3-Think (32B) among the models

F19.quote: OLMoTrace can be applied to any LM as long as the service provider has access to its full training data.
F19.claim: applicable to any language model, on the condition that the service provider has access to its full training data

F20.quote: However, Liu reasons that closed model providers may hesitate to use OLMoTrace because it would expose the training data to sunlight.
F20.claim: Liu, reported: closed-model providers may hesitate to use it because it would expose their training data

F21.quote: We showcase how it can be used to explore fact checking, hallucination, and the creativity of language models.
F21.claim: uses shown by the authors: exploring fact checking, hallucination and creativity
F21.lineage: uses: fact checking, hallucination, creativity, math

F22.quote: We present three case studies for ways to use OLMoTrace (§ 5 ): (1) fact checking, (2) tracing the LM-generated “creative” expressions, and (3) tracing math capabilities.
F22.claim: three case studies, fact checking first, then 'creative' expressions and math capabilities
F22.lineage: uses: fact checking, hallucination, creativity, math

F23.quote: If the LM states a fact, users may be able to fact-check the statement against its training data.
F23.claim: fact checking stated as a possibility: users may be able to fact-check a model's statement against its training data
F23.lineage: fact checking: what a matched document can and cannot show

F24.quote: If the LM states a fact, users may be able to fact-check the statement against its training data.
F24.claim: the published version carries the same conditional
F24.lineage: fact checking: what a matched document can and cannot show
F24.checked_against: saved text B3.txt (sha256 26daccd5e52cd634…), B3-pdf.txt (sha256 f2fc53f52892169d…), whitespace-normalised

F25.quote: We note that inspecting the document context and source can help users make a more informed judgment on the factuality of the statement, as words can be misleading out of context, and some web sources may be unreliable.
F25.claim: its qualification: the document's context and source help a more informed judgment, since words mislead out of context and some sources are unreliable
F25.lineage: fact checking: what a matched document can and cannot show

F26.quote: The interpretation of text matches with training data is quite nuanced. For some highlighted spans in the model response, we can use their corresponding documents to fact check claims made in the spans.
F26.claim: the operator's post: interpreting matches is 'quite nuanced'; for some spans the documents can be used to fact-check the span's claims
F26.lineage: fact checking: what a matched document can and cannot show

F27.quote: If you personally verify that these documents come from trusted sources, you can gain confidence that this piece of information generated by the model is factually correct.
F27.claim: confidence in a generated fact is conditional on the user personally verifying that the matched documents come from trusted sources
F27.lineage: fact checking: what a matched document can and cannot show

F28.quote: Called OLMoTrace, it's an open-source application offering fact-checking of information provided in prompt replies.
F28.claim: the newsletter: an open-source application offering fact-checking of replies
F28.lineage: fact checking: what a matched document can and cannot show

F29.quote: anyone using our models can ensure that the data supporting their outputs is trustworthy and verifiable.
F29.claim: Liu, in Ai2's launch statement: users can ensure that the data 'supporting their outputs' is trustworthy and verifiable
F29.lineage: fact checking: what a matched document can and cannot show

F30.locus: ¶ 'OLMoTrace connects the output to the input' (Farhadi)
F30.quote: And the minute you start linking the generation to an input—assuming that the inputs were factual—then you can start also cooking up scores for hallucination
F30.claim: Farhadi, reported: once generation is linked to input, and assuming the inputs factual, hallucination scores become possible
F30.lineage: uses: fact checking, hallucination, creativity, math

F31.quote: OLMoTrace reveals that this entire expression appears multiple times in the training data, so the model could have easily learned it through memorization.
F31.claim: a math expression found many times in the training data: the model could have learned it by memorization
F31.lineage: uses: fact checking, hallucination, creativity, math

F32.quote: now we can see that the model may have learned to say August 2023 from the post-training examples listed on the right. This finding led us to remove contents containing knowledge cutoff dates from the 32B model’s post-training data.
F32.claim: a false knowledge-cutoff claim traced to post-training examples; the finding changed the 32B model's post-training data
F32.lineage: uses: fact checking, hallucination, creativity, math

F33.locus: ¶ 'As we start to look towards regulation' (Lebrecht)
F33.quote: As we start to look towards regulation, governance, and auditability, there are certain key sectors right now that are limited in what they can deploy at scale with black-box models,
F33.claim: Lebrecht, reported: regulation, governance and auditability limit what key sectors can deploy with black-box models; traceability as a pathway

F34.quote: OLMoTrace finds lexical, verbatim matches between an LM’s output and its training data. The retrieved documents should not be interpreted as having a causal effect on the LM output, or as supporting evidence or citations for the LM output.
F34.claim: the authors' stated limit: lexical, verbatim matches only; the documents are not causes of the output, and not supporting evidence or citations for it
F34.lineage: the stated limit: not causes, not evidence, not citations

F35.quote: The retrieved documents should not be interpreted as having a causal effect on the LM output, or as supporting evidence or citations for the LM output.
F35.claim: the published version (ACL 2025) carries the same limit
F35.lineage: the stated limit: not causes, not evidence, not citations
F35.checked_against: saved text B3.txt (sha256 26daccd5e52cd634…), B3-pdf.txt (sha256 f2fc53f52892169d…), whitespace-normalised

F36.quote: Ai2 doesn't intend for the documents retrieved to be viewed as the definitive source of the model's learning. "We're just showing you some associations, connections between them. Some of them may warrant a further inspection," Liu clarified.
F36.claim: the newsletter and Liu: the documents are not the definitive source of the model's learning, only associations, some warranting inspection
F36.lineage: the stated limit: not causes, not evidence, not citations

F37.locus: ¶ 'In an example where OLMo was asked about the Space Needle'
F37.quote: Ai2 asserts that OLMOTrace’s results should not be mistaken as indicators of authority.
F37.claim: Ai2, reported: the results are not indicators of authority (a matched blog ranks beside an official site)
F37.lineage: the stated limit: not causes, not evidence, not citations

F38.quote: OLMoTrace doesn't provide analytics or insights to help developers determine what to do next to improve the training data. Simply put, it's generating awareness.
F38.claim: the newsletter's own assessment: it tags where data came from and gives no analytics for improving the training data; it generates awareness

F39.quote: Examples of them include Bing Chat, Google AI Overview, and Perplexity AI. Despite looking similar, OLMoTrace is fundamentally different from RAG: OLMoTrace retrieves documents post-hoc and does not intervene with the LM generation.
F39.claim: set against retrieval-augmented generation, Google AI Overview named among its examples: OLMoTrace retrieves post hoc and does not intervene in generation

F40.quote: We are not intervening with the model response. Our response is purely generated by the neural language model.
F40.claim: Liu, reported: unlike Perplexity's retrieval, OLMoTrace does not intervene in the model's response

F41.quote: the Gemini App has a “double-check response” feature that highlights parts of the LM response and shows similar results from Google Search, which is updated in real time and thus not identical to Gemini’s training data, making it less useful for scientific exploration.
F41.claim: Gemini's 'double-check response' shows Google Search results that are not Gemini's training data, less useful for scientific exploration
